prompt: Complete TypedSettingsReader so it pulls Integers, Strings and Booleans out of a Map<String, Object> without ever throwing ClassCastException, recording the keys whose values had the wrong type.
explanation: Casting an Object is only safe behind an instanceof guard; the guard turns a crash into a value your caller can handle. The exercise also separates two different failures that are easy to confuse: a key that is absent is normal and silent, while a key whose value has the wrong type is a configuration mistake worth reporting. Returning a copy from problems() stops callers from editing the reader's own record.
hints: Fetch the value once into an Object variable, return the fallback immediately if it is null, and only then test its type.
'raw instanceof Integer number' both checks the type and gives you the unboxed value to return.
Add the key to the problem list in the branch that runs when the type test fails -- not when the key is missing.
